# dsh-quberi

Query your Quberi knowledge base from DeepSeek Harness:
search, browse, save notes and upload files.

The interesting part isn't the search — it's what search is allowed to return.
Quberi enforces permi

ssions **per document**, not per space: two people asking
the same question in the same space can ge

t different answers, because the
retrieval filter runs inside the vector index and a denied document

is never a
candidate in the first place.

- Per-document access rules with **deny wins** — a grant cannot override a
decision to hide one docu

ment.
- **Filtered at retrieval time**, so you get a full result set, not a shorter
one with holes.

- **Revoked picture links die** — a picture preview URL issued before access was
removed returns 404

on the next request.
- Writes go only into spaces you can edit; uploads require your confirmation
e

ext request.
- Writes go only into spaces you can edit; uploads require your confirmation
each time.

Ask Harness a question about your documents. The first time, your browser
opens by itself so you can

approve access; after that the model can call
`quberi_search`, which finds passages in the document

s **you** can read in
Quberi, in the one organization you pick (name a space to search only that one

). It can also call `quberi_save` to add
a note (a conclusion, decision or summary from the chat) to

your knowledge base,
and `quberi_upload_file` to add a file from your workspace. `quberi_list_space

s`
and `quberi_list_documents` show what is there, and `quberi_search_images` finds
pictures from a

description and shows them in the chat. Saving is new in 0.3.0
and uploading in 0.4.0; each needs a

fresh sign-in that includes it. Browsing and
picture search need nothing beyond search. An
upload on
ly happens after **you approve that file** (see Uploading files).
[该节后续省略]
## Install
In DeepSeek Harness open **Plugins → Add plugin** and enter:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Or from a terminal (replace `desktop` with your profile name):
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Then restart Harness. To upgrade, remove the old version first
(`dsh plugin --profile desktop remove
dsh-quberi`), then add it again.

You need a Quberi account at ai.quberi.com, or your own
Quberi server (see Configuration).

A plugin runs on your machine with your permissions, so read the source first.
It is small: `src/oau

th.ts` (sign-in helpers), `src/browser.ts` (opens your
browser), `src/controller.ts` (sign-in, token

refresh, search, save, upload),
`src/upload.ts` (which files may be uploaded, and the approval gate

s` (the `/quberi` command and the tools). Its only runtime
dependency is `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`.
### From source
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Use
| Command | What it does |
| `/quberi login` | Opens your browser to sign in to Quberi (the link is also shown in case it does
not open). Choose an organization and allow. You rarely need this: the first search does it for you.

If you signed in with an older version, run it again to allow saving or uploading. |
| `/quberi sta

tus` | Shows whether you are connected. Never prints a token. |
| `/quberi logout` | Revokes the sig

n-in at Quberi and forgets it locally. |
| `/quberi mode [text\|image\|both]` | Shows or sets where
searches look: the documents' text, pictures, or both (the default). See Where a search looks. |

The sign-in page says what Harness is asking to do (search, save notes, upload files) and
what it ca
nnot do, and lets you choose the organization (shown here in Chinese):
You can also disconnect any time in Quberi under **Account → Connected tools**.

When sign-in finishes, the browser shows a confirmation page and Harness is
brought back to the fron
t (macOS). Nothing needs to be copied or pasted.

On a machine with no screen (a remote shell), the browser is not opened; the
plugin gives you the li
nk to open on another device instead.
## What leaves Quberi

The passages the search returns go to Harness and to whichever AI model Harness
uses. Quberi's "chec

k before sending" step does not apply to this path. Every
search is recorded in the organization's a

udit log (the tool's name and the
documents returned, never the question or the text).

`quberi_read_around` sends more of a document than the search does: up to 3000 characters on
either

side of a passage, only when the model asks for it, and only from documents you can open
in Quberi.

Each call is recorded in the audit log (the document, the version and how many
characters, never the

text) and is rate limited. A page image is fetched by Harness from a
short-lived link on your Quber

i address; the link names one page for you and stops working when
you sign out of the tool, lose acc

ess to the document or after about ten minutes. An organization
owner can turn outside tools off, wh
ich ends all of this at once.
## What it can and cannot do

- It acts as you: search only reads spaces you can read, and save only writes
into spaces you can ed

it. Both are re-checked on every call. If your access
changes, the next call reflects it.
- It can a

dd notes and files, nothing else. It cannot edit or delete anything
that is already there.
- Saving

(`knowledge:write`) and uploading (`knowledge:upload`) are separate
permissions. A sign-in made by a

n earlier version does not have them and is
not upgraded behind your back; run `/quberi login` to ad

d them.
- Access tokens last one hour and refresh on their own; a sign-in lasts at most
90 days. A r

efresh token that is used twice is treated as stolen and the whole
sign-in is revoked.
- Turning out

side tools off for the organization, or disconnecting in Quberi,
stops the very next search or save.
## Compatibility

Built and tested against `@deepseek-ai/*` `0.2.0-rc.2`. Harness is a developer
preview and its plugi

n interfaces can change. The token set is stored with the
credential-record API (`credentials.modify

Record`) so two Harness processes
cannot overwrite each other's rotated refresh token.
